source_name: NBRM – Other institutions responsible for regulation and supervision of financial institutions
why_relevant: Regulator-curated actor map: the central bank's own list of the other MK financial supervisors (ISA/ASO, SEC, MAPAS, Deposit Insurance Fund, MoF). Best single seed for snowballing the full supervisory perimeter without guessing acronyms.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine – CDX API over nbrm.mk / slvesnik.com.mk / MK bank domains
why_relevant: The core capability of this cell: proves when a supervisory circular, deadline or rulebook version first appeared and when it was replaced. CDX gives a queryable index (timestamp, digest, status) so version changes can be detected without re-scraping the live, WAF-protected regulator site; Save Page Now can force a snapshot at the moment of discovery.

source_name: archive.today / archive.ph mirrors of MK regulator and bank pages
why_relevant: Second-line archive that captures JS-rendered and WAF-protected pages the Wayback crawler often misses on .nspx CMS sites; useful redundancy for proving a deadline was announced on a given date.

source_name: ЈП Службен весник на РСМ – free access to issues (БЕСПЛАТЕН ПРИСТАП ДО ИЗДАНИЈА)
why_relevant: Official Gazette is the legally binding publication point: a banking/payments obligation exists from its gazette date. The free-issue page exposes PDF issues directly, giving a defensible primary record of enactment dates and transition deadlines.

source_name: ЈП Службен весник – archived issues back-catalogue (Архивирани изданија)
why_relevant: Back-catalogue of historical gazette issues (including pre-2019 'Службен весник на РМ' and older NRM series). Needed to reconstruct the amendment chain behind any current banking/payments obligation and to date obligations that predate live web monitoring.

source_name: mkopen.org – third-party mirror/catalogue of .gov.mk open data
why_relevant: Independent catalogue/mirror of Macedonian government open datasets — a fallback when data.gov.mk is unreachable (as it was in this run) and a way to see datasets that were later withdrawn from the official portal.

source_name: Ministry of Finance – 'Отворени финансии' open finance portal & news
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance is co-legislator for financial-sector statutes and publishes dataset updates through the Open Finance portal; its news feed is the earliest official signal that a financial law is going to consultation and that data releases have been refreshed.

source_name: State Statistical Office – National Summary Data Page (SDDS)
source_subtype: statistical release calendar / summary data page
why_relevant: IMF SDDS National Summary Data Page: a standardised, stable-URL page carrying key macro-financial indicators with fixed release calendars. Stable structure makes it a low-maintenance durable monitoring endpoint and a cross-check on NBRM release timing.

source_name: Government of RNM – Open Government / Open Data section (vlada.mk)
why_relevant: Government-level pointer to the open-data policy, OGP commitments and the data.gov.mk portal; useful for anticipating new publication obligations (e.g. which institutions are being mandated to publish machine-readable data next) that create future A3 endpoints.

source_name: MDT portal – compendium 'Закони кои го регулираат финансискиот систем'
why_relevant: A government-published compendium enumerating the statutes governing the MK financial system — an instant, authoritative checklist of every law an A3 run must track (banking, payment services, AML, insurance, securities), with the exact official titles needed for gazette and ENER keyword matching.

source_name: Собрание на РСМ — Детали за седница / session materials (bill tracker)
why_relevant: Per-sitting agenda and attached материјали — this is where a Предлог-закон за изменување и дополнување на Законот за банките / за платежни услуги и платни системи actually appears with its text, amandmani and committee reports before adoption. Primary bill-tracking surface for the cell.

source_name: Собрание на РСМ — Работни тела (parliamentary committees)
why_relevant: Committee stage (notably Комисија за финансирање и буџет and Комисија за економски прашања) is where banking/payments bills are debated in прво читање and where amendments are tabled. Committee agendas and reports are the earliest public sighting of substantive text changes and of any shortened procedure that compresses deadlines.

source_name: Парламентарен институт при Собранието — истражувања и кратки информации
why_relevant: The Assembly's research service publishes 'кратка информација' / 'нацрт закон' briefing papers on bills before MPs. These summarise the policy problem, EU-acquis reference and comparative practice — useful for understanding why a banking or payments statute is being changed, and they occasionally reveal bills not yet visible elsewhere. Confirmed to exist (e.g. a 2024 briefing PDF under /content/ПИ 2024-Истражувања/).

source_name: Влада на РСМ — Седници на Влада (government session agendas and outcomes)
why_relevant: The Government is the proposer of nearly every banking/payments statute. 'Утврден е Предлог-закон ...' in a session readout is the moment a bill leaves the executive and enters Parliament — the single most reliable handoff signal between the ЕНЕР stage and the Собрание stage. Session numbering also allows a complete, gap-checkable series.

source_name: Влада на РСМ — Соопштенија (press releases, incl. ENER publication notices)
why_relevant: Government press releases announce when a draft law is put on ЕНЕР and how long the consultation runs (confirmed pattern, e.g. 'Предлогот на Законот за кривичната постапка е објавен на ЕНЕР'). Gives a low-cost push signal for consultations that would otherwise require polling ЕНЕР itself.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Закони и прописи / Закони
why_relevant: The ministry that drafts banking, payment-services, FX and financial-stability statutes maintains its own consolidated list of laws in force, with a dedicated 'Закони кои го регулираат финансискиот систем' sub-page. Useful as the authoritative mapping from statute to responsible drafter, and as a cross-check that a gazette amendment has been absorbed.

source_name: arhiva.finance.gov.mk — Ministry of Finance legacy archive of gazette-published acts
why_relevant: Hosts PDFs of gazette-published statutes retaining the 'Службен весник на РСМ, бр. NNN од DD.MM.YYYY' header (confirmed for the 2025 Budget Execution Law, Сл. весник 254/16.12.2024). Practical fallback for gazette text when slvesnik.com.mk is unreachable, and a source of historical issue-number/date pairs.

source_name: Стопанска комора на Северна Македонија (Economic Chamber) — draft-law document library
why_relevant: The Chamber circulates draft laws to members for comment and posts the actual PDFs — confirmed to hold 'Предлог за изменување и дополнување на Законот за банките' carrying the Службен весник бр. 37 од 19.2.2025 header, and NBRM decisions. It is a de-facto mirror for gazette and bill text that is more crawlable than the primary sites, and its circulation letters reveal industry consultation timelines.

source_name: Управа за финансиско разузнавање (Financial Intelligence Office) — Закони од областа на спречување перење пари
why_relevant: Authoritative statute page for the AML/CFT limb of the cell: hosts the unofficial consolidated text of Законот за спречување перење пари и финансирање на тероризам with amendment history (base text Сл. весник 120/2018; amending law adopted 3.10.2024, published Сл. весник 208 од 9.10.2024). Consolidated texts here are the fastest way to see which articles a gazette amendment actually touched.

source_name: Уставен суд на Република Северна Македонија (Constitutional Court)
why_relevant: The only body that can strike down a published statute or a bank-related bylaw, so it is the tail risk on any compliance deadline. Confirmed to have handled banking-sector initiatives (У.бр.42/2021 on the temporary dividend-distribution restriction on banks; У.бр.17/2021 on a bank statute; У.бр.247/2020 on deposits and property rights). Filings (иницијативи) also surface industry objections to new statutes months before any ruling.

source_name: Министерство/Секретаријат за европски прашања — НПАА (National Programme for Adoption of the EU Acquis)
why_relevant: The NPAA is the government's forward legislative calendar: it names, per acquis chapter (Ch. 4 free movement of capital, Ch. 9 financial services, Ch. 24 justice/freedom/security for AML), which laws will be drafted or amended and by when. Best available source for banking/payments statutes that do not yet exist as bills. Note the institution was reorganised from Секретаријат (sep.gov.mk) to Министерство за европски прашања (mep.gov.mk) — both hosts serve NPAA pages with matching post ids.

source_name: Огледало на Владата (Mirror of the Government) — ENER monitoring by MCIC/CRC
why_relevant: Civil-society monitor that publishes weekly, monthly and quarterly reviews of every draft law posted to ЕНЕР, plus explanatory resources on the законодавна постапка and ПВР cycle. Two functions for this cell: (a) a ready-made push digest of new consultations, and (b) a calibration source on how much never reaches ЕНЕР — their finding that only ~51% of 2023 government bills were published there is the key reliability caveat for treating ЕНЕР as complete coverage.

source_name: AKADEMIKA — commercial consolidated legal database (Академик)
why_relevant: The main commercial consolidation service for RNM law: daily-updated, claims full coverage of laws in force plus ~17,500 bylaws, with amendment histories tied to gazette issues. For a compliance-deadline workflow it removes the need to reconstruct consolidated text from successive gazette amendments. Registration/subscription required — licence terms must be checked before any automated collection.

source_name: Правдико (Pravdiko) — free law base and legal news
why_relevant: Free, openly crawlable mirror of statute texts ('База на закони') with dated PDF filenames, plus legal-news coverage of bills. Confirmed to host statute PDFs bearing the Собрание header. Useful as an open fallback where slvesnik and akademika are blocked, and as an early-warning news feed on legislative moves — but it is a secondary compiler, so treat text as indicative and confirm against the gazette.

source_name: Library of Congress — Guide to Law Online: North Macedonia (Legislative)
why_relevant: Curated, maintained English-language index of the official legislative sources for RNM (gazette, Assembly, legal databases). Valuable as a snowball seed and as a stable cross-check when official portals rename sections; not a content source itself.
